newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Reuters to return cash via dividends.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Reuters to return cash via dividends.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it proposed to return 613 million pounds ($953.3 million) of cash to shareholders over three years through a bonus issue of a new class of special dividend shares.
Under the proposal and a share capital consolidation, shareholders will receive 19 ordinary shares and one special dividend share for every 20 shares held on October 8.

Each special dividend share will pay net dividends totalling 750 pence over three years, which compares with an average Reuters share price of 752 pence for the week to September 9, the international news and information organisation said.

Reuters had previously said it was looking at ways of returning surplus cash to shareholders. However, in the statement it said, "It was not possible to repeat the share repurchase structure which was adopted in 1993."
It said UK tax clearance was not available for such a structure this time and added that it had not received comprehensive clearance for its current proposal.
However it had received the required clearance for the company itself and also for its U.S. shareholders, who account for 32 percent of its total shareholder base.
The company believed, based on advice, that the proposal avoided any tax disadvantage for existing shareholders in respect of their current holdings, the Reuters statement added.
Reuters shares rose on news of the cash distribution, hitting a high for the day of 787p before easing back to trade 16p higher at 766 by 1305 GMT.

Reuters said the share capital consolidation allowed easy comparison with past performance of both earnings per share (EPS) and the ordinary share price and said it was not expected to have any significant impact on EPS.
The consolidation results in a five percent reduction in the number of ordinary shares in issue, the company said.

Under the scheme, holders of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), will receive one special dividend American Depositary Share (ADS) and 19 new ADSs for every 20 ADSs held at the close of business on 8 October 1996.
Reuters said the payment will not diminish its high levels of investment for future growth.
"We don't feel that it in any way diminishes our ability to invest in organic growth or, if appropriate, to make acquisitions," the company spokesman said.

"The key thing is that we're distributing 613 million pounds over three years. At a rate of around 200 million pounds a year... that's not far off the rate at which we have been generating cash," the spokesman said. "So we will still have substantial cash resources," he added.
Reuters said at the time of its half-year results in July that its cash balances had grown to 866 million pounds and it was seeking to resolve ways of distributing surplus cash.
"The company considers the proposal to be the best way of enabling shareholders to receive more cash, more efficiently, at a faster rate and on an equal basis," it said.
It said an on-market share repurchase was effectively ruled out because of the high proportion of holders in the U.S. and the board's objective of treating all shareholders equally.
Each special dividend share will pay six net dividends over the next three years of 125p each, giving total special dividends per share of 750p, the company said.
Reuters has applied for the special dividend shares to be listed in the Britain and the ADSs in the U.S. Trading in these shares is expected to begin on October 10.
The company said the proposal will result in the company having returned nearly one billion pounds of cash to shareholders in the 1990s, in addition to ordinary dividends.
An extraordinary general meeting of the company to vote on the proposal has been set for October 9.

SBC Warburg is independently offering to shareholders outside the U.S., Canada, Australia and Japan a special share dealing facility in Britain for the special dividend shares, the company added. ($1=.6430 Pound)
